blocks.what_we_do: Learn how [population structure](../docs/glossary.md#population-stratification) can mislead an association study. Then look at the reference samples we will use.
blocks.why:
Cases and controls may be recruited from groups with different ancestry. Ancestry means the broad genetic background that a person inherits from their forebears. Then the [allele frequency](../docs/glossary.md#allele-frequency) (how common an allele is in a group) can differ between cases and controls, even at sites that have nothing to do with the disease. This is called [confounding](../docs/glossary.md#confounding): a hidden factor is linked to both the group and the genetics.

A PC is a single number per person that summarises one main direction of genetic variation across many sites. Principal component analysis (PCA) is the method that finds these directions. PCA only describes patterns. Its axes are not diagnoses, nationality or ethnicity. The reference labels are background information, not a ranking of people. We define an ancestry-matched teaching cohort before we look at any association p-values.
blocks.you_need: The saved state from the end of module 4. You also need the supplied GRCh38 [reference subset](../docs/glossary.md#reference-subset), which comes with the course package.
blocks.command:
```{r s5-1}
reference <- file.path(cfg$data_dir, "pca_reference", "ref1000g_grch38")
reference_samples <- guided_table(paste0(reference, ".psam"))
table(reference_samples$SuperPop)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

Not applicable: this step needs no PLINK command. The R chunk is the complete command.

R reads or calculates the displayed values without changing the genotype files.

The chunk reads the sample table of the reference (a [.psam file](../docs/glossary.md#pvar-psam-files)) and counts the samples in each group.
blocks.expected_result:
This supplied subset has 1,062 samples labelled EUR, AFR, EAS and SAS. The labels describe where the reference samples were collected. The table shows only the groups present in this subset, not every possible 1000 Genomes group.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message and the previous step. Keep the command and the console log. Do not use files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Can an allele-frequency difference between cases and controls appear because their ancestry differs, even when the site has no effect on the disease?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

Yes. Ancestry can influence both which group a person is in and which alleles that person carries.

</details>
